paragraphs.text: Your objectives remain unchanged from the last review: to achieve long-term growth, with no requirement for income from the portfolio for the foreseeable future. Both of you continue to be comfortable with maintaining a moderate risk level.
Your agreed risk profile is moderate (4).
We discussed using the £120,000 inheritance, together with the full value of your joint General Investment Account, to fund your investments.
The proposed source of funds is Jean's inheritance and the joint General Investment Account.
The recommendations discussed are to top up both Robert's and Jean's ISAs for the new tax year, and to open a new joint investment account for any remaining funds.
The recommendation involves selling down existing investments.
We agreed to disinvest the joint General Investment Account and, together with the inheritance, fund both ISAs and open a new jointly-held investment account for the balance.

Jean has received an inheritance of about £120,000, which has now cleared. You would like to invest this alongside your existing portfolio.

The recommended investment amount is £120,000 from the inheritance, plus the full value of the joint General Investment Account. The sources of funds are the inheritance from Jean and the joint General Investment Account.
Selling down your General Investment Account is considered a disposal, which may result in a capital gains tax position to be assessed against your annual exempt amount.
